paragraphs.paragraph: The Prophecy to the Mountains of Israel
paragraphs.title: The Prophecy to the Mountains of Israel

easy.explanation: The Lord told Ezekiel to set his face toward the mountains of Israel.
easy.q: To whom was Ezekiel commanded to direct his prophecy?

easy.explanation: They were told to hear the word of the Lord God.
easy.q: What were the mountains of Israel told to hear?

easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I ... will bring a sword upon you.”
easy.q: What did the Lord say He would bring upon the mountains?

medium.explanation: The verse addresses the mountains, hills, rivers, and valleys.
medium.q: What other features of the land are addressed along with the mountains?

medium.explanation: He declares, “I will destroy your high places.”
medium.q: What does the Lord say He will destroy?

answers: A raised site used for worship
medium.explanation: The context connects high places with altars and idolatrous worship.
medium.q: In the passage, what is a “high place”?

answers: They stand for the land and its worship sites
They are described as living creatures
challenge.explanation: Addressing the mountains presents the judgment as reaching throughout the land.
challenge.q: Why may the mountains represent more than the physical hills themselves?

answers: The sword will accompany their destruction
The sword will be placed in them for worship
challenge.explanation: The Lord brings the sword upon the land and declares the destruction of its high places.
challenge.q: How are the sword and the high places connected?

answers: The landscape becomes the symbolic audience of the prophecy
The prophecy is limited to Ezekiel
challenge.explanation: The direct address makes the land itself a symbolic focus of judgment.
challenge.q: What is the effect of speaking directly to the mountains?

paragraphs.idea: The Prophecy to the Mountains of Israel

paragraphs.paragraph: The Destruction of Idolatrous Worship Places
paragraphs.title: The Destruction of Idolatrous Worship Places

answers: They will be moved to Egypt
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “your altars shall be desolate.”
easy.q: What will happen to the altars?

easy.explanation: The Lord says He will cast the slain before their idols.
easy.q: Before whom will the slain men be cast down?

easy.explanation: The cities shall be laid waste in all the dwellingplaces.
easy.q: What will happen to the cities?

medium.explanation: The Lord says, “I will scatter your bones round about your altars.”
medium.q: Where will the bones of Israel be scattered?

answers: They will be broken and cut down
They will be carried into the wilderness
medium.explanation: The passage says the images and idols will be broken, cut down, and cease.
medium.q: What will happen to the images and idols?

answers: The people’s idolatrous practices will be ended
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the ending of the sinful works associated with the worship sites.
medium.q: What does “your works may be abolished” mean in context?

answers: It shows that the idols cannot save their worshipers
It shows that the idols won a victory
It protects the idols from destruction
challenge.explanation: Their worshipers die before images that have no power to deliver them.
challenge.q: Why is it significant that the slain fall before the idols?

answers: Cities are built and altars are honored
Cities are laid waste and idolatrous sites are destroyed
The people return and rebuild the high places
challenge.explanation: The passage describes ruined cities, desolate high places, and broken idols.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes these verses?

answers: Judgment is linked to the people’s idolatry
Worship sites are places of safety
The people were separated from their idols
challenge.explanation: The location of the slain directly connects the judgment with their idolatrous worship.
challenge.q: What does the repeated connection between death and worship sites emphasize?

paragraphs.idea: The Destruction of Idolatrous Worship Places

paragraphs.paragraph: The Survivors of Exile and Their Repentance
paragraphs.title: The Survivors of Exile and Their Repentance

answers: They will be scattered among the nations
They will all remain in Jerusalem
They will immediately build new cities
easy.explanation: The remnant will escape the sword among the nations and be scattered through the countries.
easy.q: What will happen to the remnant of Israel?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “they that escape of you shall remember me.”
easy.q: Whom will those who escape remember?

easy.explanation: They shall loathe themselves for the evils they committed.
easy.q: What will the survivors hate or loathe in themselves?

answers: Among the nations where they are carried captive
At the gates of their former cities
medium.explanation: They will remember Him among the nations where they are carried captive.
medium.q: Where will the survivors remember the Lord?

answers: A heart that turned away from the Lord to idols
medium.explanation: The phrase describes spiritual unfaithfulness and departure from the Lord.
medium.q: What does the phrase “whorish heart” describe?

answers: It leads the survivors to remember, understand, and loathe their sins
It removes all memory of their past
medium.explanation: In exile they remember the Lord and recognize the evil of their actions.
medium.q: How does exile contribute to repentance?

answers: It includes correction as well as punishment
It is only an act of revenge
It has no connection with their sins
challenge.explanation: Their remembrance and remorse show that judgment can lead to correction.
challenge.q: What does the survivors’ repentance reveal about the purpose of judgment?

answers: Remembering the Lord leads them to recognize their evil
Remembering the Lord makes them proud
They are unrelated in the passage
challenge.explanation: Their remembrance brings recognition of sin and hatred of their former deeds.
challenge.q: How are remembrance of the Lord and shame related?

answers: The announced judgment had a real purpose and cause
The prophecy was spoken without meaning
The judgment was intended only for foreign nations
challenge.explanation: The statement assures that the threatened evil was neither empty nor without cause.
challenge.q: What does “I have not said in vain” emphasize?

paragraphs.idea: The Survivors of Exile and Their Repentance

answers: Smite with his hand and stamp with his foot
Raise a banner over the city
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded him to smite with his hand and stamp with his foot.
easy.q: What was Ezekiel commanded to do?

easy.explanation: The far-off person would die of the pestilence.
easy.q: By what would the person far away die?

easy.explanation: The one who remained and was besieged would die by famine.
easy.q: By what would the person who remained and was besieged die?

answers: Grief and alarm at the coming judgment
medium.explanation: The dramatic gestures accompany his lament over Israel’s evil and punishment.
medium.q: What do Ezekiel’s striking and stamping express?

answers: The far-off face pestilence, the near face the sword, and the besieged face famine
The far-off face famine and the near face pestilence
medium.explanation: The verse assigns pestilence, sword, and famine to three different groups.
medium.q: How are the three forms of judgment distributed?

medium.explanation: A besieged person is enclosed by an enemy and unable to leave freely.
medium.q: What does “besieged” mean in this passage?

answers: The punishment reaches people in different circumstances
Only one small group will suffer
The judgment is described without detail
challenge.explanation: The passage includes those far away, those near, and those trapped under siege.
challenge.q: What does the threefold judgment show?

answers: Both express distress over Israel’s evil and coming fall
challenge.explanation: The gestures and cry together communicate deep grief and alarm.
challenge.q: How do Ezekiel’s gestures relate to his cry of “Alas”?

answers: They will know that the Lord is God
They will worship the idols more confidently
challenge.explanation: The chapter repeatedly connects the judgment with knowing that He is the Lord.
challenge.q: What knowledge follows the judgment described in the passage?

paragraphs.paragraph: The Slain at the Worship Sites and the Desolation of the Land
paragraphs.title: The Slain at the Worship Sites and the Desolation of the Land

answers: Among their idols and around their altars
easy.explanation: The slain will be among the idols and round about the altars.
easy.q: Where will the slain be found?

answers: High hills, mountain tops, green trees, and thick oaks
easy.explanation: The passage names hills, mountains, green trees, and thick oaks.
easy.q: Which places are named as locations of idolatrous worship?

answers: It will become crowded with cities
It will be covered with palaces
easy.explanation: The Lord says He will make the land desolate in all their habitations.
easy.q: What will happen to the land?

answers: The slain will be found at the very places where idols were worshiped
The slain will protect the worship sites
medium.explanation: The slain are located among the idols, altars, hills, and trees used in worship.
medium.q: What is the connection between the slain and the worship sites?

answers: The land will be desolate throughout the settlements
medium.explanation: The land will be made desolate in all their habitations.
medium.q: What will result when the Lord stretches out His hand upon the land?

answers: A large tree with dense branches
medium.explanation: The phrase identifies a large, heavily branched tree used as a worship site.
medium.q: In context, what is a “thick oak”?

answers: Idolatrous worship had spread throughout the land
Worship occurred in only one city
The trees were enemies of Israel
challenge.explanation: The many named locations show the widespread nature of the idolatry.
challenge.q: What does the variety of worship locations suggest?

answers: It leads the people to know that the Lord is God
It prevents every kind of recognition
challenge.explanation: The final statement says, “they shall know that I am the Lord.”
challenge.q: How does the desolation of the land serve the chapter’s conclusion?

answers: The desolation will extend throughout their settlements
The judgment will affect only one village
The people will move into one city
challenge.explanation: The phrase stresses the comprehensive reach of the land’s desolation.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “in all their habitations” emphasize?

paragraphs.idea: The Slain at the Worship Sites and the Desolation of the Land
